data.body:
# Concision research — verified sources and calibrated recommendations

## What the 2026 evidence supports

The direct evidence does not justify a universal small word cap. It supports selective compression with explicit fact preservation and downstream-cost evaluation.

- [Valid ≠ Necessary: Diagnosing Latent Inefficiency in Chain-of-Thought](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11266) introduces Context-Aware Information Density and PACE; PACE cuts reasoning tokens 31–53% on three benchmarks while maintaining accuracy. Transfer to tickets: validity/completeness is not the same as necessity; score contribution to the durable objective.
- [When LLMs Over-Answer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17063) reports redundant alternatives in 65.7% and padding in 69.1% of a 6,246-item HDL Q&A corpus. Transfer: require one chosen answer/plan and distinguish core from non-core content. This is domain-specific Q&A evidence, not ticket evidence.
- [The Sleeping Agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11775) shows gist compression discarded temporal facts; adding one explicit preservation instruction raised temporal-expression retention from 3.05% to 62.39%. Transfer: enumerate protected fact classes rather than merely saying “be concise.”
- [What Does Context Compression Cost an Agent?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16370) shows completion can remain statistically unchanged while retrieval calls rise sharply when execution state is dropped. Transfer: evaluate rereads/tool calls and resumption success, not only completion or length.
- [On Problems of Implicit Context Compression for Software Engineering Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11051) reports a compression technique that works on single-shot understanding but fails on multi-step coding. Transfer: durable execution state needs a higher preservation floor than a single answer.

Relevant 2025 support: [verbosity compensation](https://aclanthology.org/2025.uncertainlp-main.14/), [context length alone hurts despite perfect retrieval](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.1264/), [length bias in LLM preference evaluation](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.358/), and [token-budget-aware reasoning](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.1274/). These explain why uncertainty can cause repetition, why length-matched judging matters, and why adaptive budgets are safer than tiny fixed caps.

These are recent preprints or adjacent-domain studies. They support the design pattern, not the local numeric thresholds. The 20-ticket calibration is the local evidence for threshold behavior.

## OSS precedents

GitHub metadata checked 2026-09-03: all six repositories below were public, non-archived, had roughly 25k–281k stars, and were pushed between 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-03.

- [openai/skills — skill-creator](https://github.com/openai/skills/blob/main/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md): says the context window is a public good, asks whether each paragraph justifies its token cost, prefers concise examples, forbids duplicating SKILL.md/reference content, and uses progressive disclosure.
- [anthropics/skills — skill-creator](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md): three loading levels; metadata ~100 words, SKILL.md under 500 lines ideal, detailed resources loaded only when needed; explicitly says counts are approximate and longer is allowed when needed.
- [obra/superpowers — writing-skills](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/main/skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md): skills are reusable techniques, not narratives of one solution; mechanical checks belong in automation; concise caps, tool-help links, and cross-references reduce repeated detail. Its numeric caps are project convention, not universal evidence.
- [wshobson/agents — static evaluator](https://github.com/wshobson/agents/blob/main/plugins/plugin-eval/src/plugin_eval/layers/static.py#L384-L408): deterministically scores duplicate nonempty lines and MUST/NEVER/ALWAYS density, while token efficiency is only 9% of the composite versus progressive disclosure, structural completeness, and other dimensions. This is the right weighting instinct.
- [anthropics/claude-code — code-reviewer agent](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/plugins/feature-dev/agents/code-reviewer.md): scopes the review, reports only confidence >=80 issues, and requires each issue to carry file/line, explanation, and concrete fix; no-issue output is a brief summary. Noise is reduced by evidence/confidence gating.
- [github/awesome-copilot — Caveman Mode](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/agents/caveman-mode.agent.md): community prompt targeting 50–70% fewer tokens, no greetings/meta narration, and explicit expansion exceptions. Its 3–6-word sentences and article dropping are too rigid for accurate durable engineering text and are not official GitHub product policy.

The convergence is: every token earns a place; detail remains accessible behind links/resources; schemas and positive examples beat vague “be brief”; deterministic checks handle mechanical problems; output findings are scoped and evidence-gated.

## Guidance for agents

Use this compact policy:

“Write the minimum sufficient durable record. Preserve every fact needed to execute, verify, decide, audit, or resume: objective/current state, chosen approach, constraints and decisions, identifiers, paths, commands, values, dates, measurements, owners, blockers, exact errors, evidence, and next action. Lead with outcome or delta. Link canonical or bulky evidence instead of copying it. Remove greetings, tool narration, generic background, repeated context, unchosen alternatives, and closing restatements. Expand only for ambiguity, risk, evidence, or decision rationale.”

Operational writing pass:

1. Identify the artifact and its future reader.
2. Draft facts, not prose. Mark each semantic unit KEEP, COMPRESS, or DELETE.
3. KEEP protected facts and causal/decision rationale; COMPRESS supporting explanation; DELETE narration, recap, generic advice, and repetition.
4. Verify every protected fact survived. State uncertainty as one unknown plus the cheapest discriminating check.
5. If evidence is bulky, write an at-most-100-word finding summary and a durable link/hash; put chronology/raw evidence in session_log.
6. Test the record: can a fresh agent name current state, chosen path, constraints, proof, blocker, owner, and exact next action without rereading history?

Artifact contracts:

- Description: problem/outcome, boundaries, constraints, scope, measurable acceptance criteria. No investigation diary.
- Plan: one chosen approach, ordered actions/dependencies, material risks, verification. Alternatives belong in a decision artifact unless choice is still blocked.
- Comment: new delta only—evidence, decision, blocker, next action/owner. Do not recap the ticket.
- Handoff: current state, unresolved risks, exact resumption point. Do not replay completed work.
- Session log: verbose chronology, raw/linked evidence, intermediate research, and audit detail; tickets link to it.

Budgets are warning rails, not writing targets. A short artifact can be bloated and a long security/incident/design record can be necessary.

## Production stance after calibration

Retain the frozen R1–R10 definitions, thresholds, protected spans, and exemptions as versioned calibration-v1, but change how findings are used:

- Blocking candidates remain only objective defects: R1 at >=3 copies or >=15% duplicated unprotected prose; R3 above 50 transcript lines or 4,000 characters without <=100-word summary plus durable pointer/hash; R4 one structurally empty eligible update. Never auto-delete.
- R2, R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, and R10 remain advisory. Always report matched spans, why they fired, and the suppression route.
- Never OR all rules into a bloat verdict. In this enriched sample the OR had 30% precision and 0% specificity.
- R6 should emit span-level rewrite suggestions, not label a ticket from one >45-word sentence or >120-word paragraph. Require a calibrated density/prevalence condition before ticket-level escalation.
- R9 should say “length review requested,” not “bloated.” Do not use the 8,000-character operational admission cap as a quality verdict. Require another independent redundancy signal for escalation, use type×complexity P95 only after >=200 labeled accepted samples, and exclude marked evidence/session-log overflow.
- R2 needs a second candidate detector for asymmetric containment and superseded-section repetition; 0.80 symmetric Jaccard missed all four semantic positives. Freeze any lower threshold only after a separate labeled validation set.
- R8 should count distinct directive propositions and cautiously include emphatic equivalents such as ONLY/NO/SINGLE/BOTH; the literal three-word lexicon missed both positives. Preserve reasoned safety/compliance exceptions.
- R10 must resolve the cited revision and compare linked tickets/session logs as well as current files; current-checkout-only comparison missed both positives.
- R3/R4/R5/R7 need deliberate positive-control tickets before their recall or precision can be claimed. Their all-negative result proves only observed specificity here.

Next validation should add ordinary-length tickets and positive controls, double-label more than two shared records, freeze adjudication before threshold tuning, and evaluate on a held-out set. Measure protected-fact retention, fresh-agent resumption success, and state-reacquisition calls alongside compression.
